sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, hold position, traffic crossing right to left.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Kingsbury via the SONTEL TWO departure, RIKAS transition, climb to 6,000 feet, squawk 4703.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, expedite climb until passing flight level 180, then climb to flight level 310.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 2,500 feet, cleared for the ILS runway 33 approach, report established.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: The time is now 1352. At your present speed MAGRU is 18 minutes ahead of you. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you need.
time now 1352 / MAGRU 18 minutes ahead

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, cross MAGRU at 1405.

Just after departure from Arlen you saw a flock of large birds at about 2,000 feet, just north of the runway. You were busy with the climb checks and did not report it. Departure now calls you. Acknowledge the instruction, and report what you saw.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, Arlen Departure, radar contact, climb to flight level 190.
Approach told you to maintain 210 knots. Moderate turbulence has forced you to slow to 180 knots and you are staying at that speed. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.
180 knots / moderate turbulence

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 210 knots?

You are 12 miles from the field, but you are high and fast and you need about 18 miles of track to get down and configure for landing. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you need instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept a short approach to runway 33?

Center cleared you to climb to flight level 200. You set flight level 220 in the altitude window by mistake and you are now climbing through flight level 205. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, I show you climbing above flight level 200 — say your cleared level.

You are number four for departure at Arlen. Ground told you to expect 10 minutes, but it has now been 25. Your crew duty time requires you to be airborne by 1430, it is now 1410, and the taxi to the runway takes 12 minutes. Contact Arlen Ground. Point out the problem and request what you need.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 2 flight stages: Taxi, Departure.

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123 at Gate Bravo 4 at Arlen Airport, ready to depart for Kingsbury. You have information Quebec and runway 24 is in use. Your flow control slot for Kingsbury is 1340, and it is now 1318.

body.text: Contact Arlen Ground, request pushback and give your information letter.
Listen to the ground controller, give a full readback, and tell him what you will do.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Arlen Ground, pushback approved, face south. There's an A220 pushing at Bravo 2 right now, so hold where you are until he's clear — give me a call when you're moving.

pre.text: Situation Update Ground tells you that taxiway Alpha is congested and the taxi to runway 24 will take 28 minutes. The time is now 1318 and your slot is 1340.

body.text: Contact Arlen Ground. Point out the problem with that taxi time, and request what you need.
Listen to the ground controller and respond accordingly. Tell him what you need to know before you decide. (Your information Quebec is 25 minutes old, and your tailwind limit is 10 knots.)

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, I can give you runway 06 instead — that's about a 9-minute taxi from where you are. Runway 06 has a tailwind though. Do what you need to do.
Listen to the ground controller, then state your decision with a reason.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, the current wind is 190 at 8 knots, so that's about 7 knots of tailwind on runway 06.
Listen to the ground controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi to runway 06 via Charlie and Foxtrot, hold short of Foxtrot 1, and contact Arlen Tower on 118.35.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Arlen Tower, number two, after the Saab 340 on short final, line up and wait runway 06.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, cleared for takeoff runway 06, climb to 3,000 feet, report passing 1,800 feet.

pre.text: Situation Update You are airborne and passing 1,800 feet, climbing to 3,000 feet.

body.text: Contact Arlen Departure, report your passing altitude and request further climb.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire what that means for your arrival.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, Arlen Departure, radar contact, climb to flight level 190, direct SONTEL when able. And by the way, Kingsbury have just moved your slot to 1352 — I'm sorry about that.
You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three.

In this situation, Ground offered you runway 06 with a tailwind when your slot was about to expire. What did you need to know before you accepted it, and why? In your role as a pilot, how do you decide whether to take a runway that saves time but has a tailwind? Give an example of a time pressure you would refuse to accept, no matter what it cost the schedule.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 330 and 110 miles from Westmoor Airport. You have 1 hour 40 minutes of fuel on board.

body.text: Contact Eastvale Control and report your position.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Eastvale Control, descend to flight level 240, reduce speed to 280 knots, expect the MAGRU ONE arrival, ILS runway 33, Westmoor altimeter 29.92.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing flight level 280 you get a CABIN ALTITUDE warning. The cabin altitude is climbing through 10,000 feet and the oxygen masks are on. You must get the aircraft down to 10,000 feet. You are descending at about 4,000 feet per minute. You have 154 passengers and 6 crew, and two passengers are feeling unwell but nobody needs urgent treatment.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, tell him you are starting an emergency descent, and request a lower level.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, tell him what the problem is, and request what you need.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, roger, descend at your discretion. Be advised the minimum safe altitude on your present track is 11,500 feet for the next 30 miles.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, turn right heading 290, that will take you clear of the high ground in 15 miles, descend to 10,000 feet. Say your intentions.
Listen to the controller and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, two things — say your present rate of descent, and tell me whether anyone on board needs medical attention.
Listen to the controller. Tell him what you need to know before you decide, then state your decision with a reason.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Westmoor is 70 miles ahead, about 20 minutes at your level. Daleford is 35 miles behind you, about 11 minutes. What would you like to do?

pre.text: Situation Update You are now level at 10,000 feet. The cabin altitude has stopped climbing and the passengers are off oxygen. You have 1 hour 15 minutes of fuel on board.

body.text: Contact the controller, give him an update, state your decision, and say what you will need on arrival.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, I have Daleford weather for you — the visibility there is 800 metres in fog and they have no ILS. Westmoor is clear. I'd go to Westmoor if I were you.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 3,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 33 approach, contact Westmoor Tower on 120.55.

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
